definition: The Eriksen flankers task is a neurocognitive test in which a person responds to target visual information while ignoring surrounding distracting information. It is used to assess selective visual attention and is also used to examine response inhibition, often through reaction time and accuracy on congruent versus conflicting displays.

reasons: The packet does not define the Eriksen Flankers task structure as “responding to target visual information while ignoring surrounding distracting information”; it only states that participants “performed an Eriksen Flankers task” and discusses selective visual attention in general terms.

The packet supports that the study analyzed congruent vs incongruent reaction times (RT) and success rates (% correct), but it does not explicitly support the definition’s claim that the task is “often used to examine response inhibition” specifically “through reaction time and accuracy on congruent versus conflicting displays.”

The definition’s wording includes broader, generic uses (“often used to assess selective visual attention” and “often used to examine response inhibition”) that are not directly evidenced as general uses in the packet; the packet instead describes one specific study’s aim and analyses.
